name: Russian Armed Forces as observed in Ukraine (2022-2026)

weightNotes.aggression: Continuous offensive pressure from 2023 through 2025 despite very high losses (RUSI Meatgrinder 2023; RUSI Third Year 2025: 'highly attritional', both sides seeking to inflict maximum damage). Not higher because Russia spent mid-2022 to late 2023 on the defensive behind prepared lines.
weightNotes.maneuver: The 2022 manoeuvre plan (10-day seizure of Kyiv, RUSI Preliminary Lessons) failed and was abandoned; since then armour is 'rarely used for attempts at breakthrough' and is used as fire support (RUSI Meatgrinder). Strongly attritional.
weightNotes.flanking: Later offensives (Avdiivka 2023-24, Pokrovsk axis 2024-25) worked by slow pincers around towns rather than frontal assault on the strongest point, but at tactical depth only; low-middling.
weightNotes.siegePreference: Campaign shaped as the reduction of fortified towns one at a time: Mariupol 2022, Sievierodonetsk/Lysychansk 2022, Bakhmut 2022-23, Avdiivka 2024, under artillery and glide-bomb (FAB-500 with UMPK kits, RUSI Meatgrinder) bombardment.
weightNotes.reserveUse: RUSI Preliminary Lessons: the 2022 plan had 'no reversionary courses of action' and reserves were thin; later mobilisation (2022) and contract recruiting fed rotations, but forces are committed piecemeal to sustain pressure. Low.
weightNotes.scouting: Poor in 2022 (culturally vulnerable to deception, RUSI). By 2023 Orlan-10 and other UAVs were tightly tied to fires through the Strelets system (RUSI Meatgrinder), and drone reconnaissance is now pervasive. Middling-high.
weightNotes.retreatThreshold: RUSI Preliminary Lessons: 'a culture of reinforcing failure unless orders are changed at higher levels'; disposable assault infantry absorbs very uneven casualties (Meatgrinder). Yet the Kyiv (March 2022) and Kherson (November 2022) withdrawals were orderly. High tolerance, held at 0.3 so it stays below modern breakpoints.
weightNotes.combinedArms: RUSI Preliminary Lessons: capabilities that should magnify one another 'must be employed sequentially', fratricide and poor EW deconfliction, land component dominant over air. BTGs failed as combined arms units and were replaced by functional infantry groupings (Meatgrinder). Partly improved reconnaissance-strike complex keeps it above 0.3.
weightNotes.initiative: RUSI Preliminary Lessons: culturally averse to giving subordinates context to exercise judgement, dishonest reporting culture, weak junior leadership. Adaptation is centralised and reactive (Meatgrinder).
weightNotes.logisticsDiscipline: Rail-bound logistics: the 2022 Kyiv axis outran its supply (stalled columns) and GMLRS strikes destroyed depots in July 2022; afterwards headquarters and depots were pulled back out of range and operations stayed close to railheads (RUSI Meatgrinder). Averaged across the war.

summary: An artillery-centric force that fights attritional battles. After the failed 2022 coup-de-main on Kyiv it reorganised from Battalion Tactical Groups into functional groupings: disposable and assault infantry probe and skirmish to locate Ukrainian positions, which are then destroyed by artillery, mortars, glide bombs and FPV drones cued by Orlan-type UAVs; armour gives fire support rather than breakthrough. On defence it builds deep engineered belts (minefields, ditches, concrete trenches) backed by dense electronic warfare. Strategically it runs a missile and drone campaign against Ukraine's energy grid and cities.
whyItWorked: Mass and firepower: in June 2022 Russia had about a 10:1 advantage in volume of fire (RUSI Preliminary Lessons). Engineering and minefields defeated Ukraine's 2023 counteroffensive (RUSI Stormbreak: deliberate assaults advanced only 700-1,200 m every five days). Russia adapts centrally and fast enough on recurring problems (thermal camouflage, EW against drones, glide bombs) and has mobilised industry and manpower to sustain a war of attrition.
whereItFailed: Kyiv 2022: a 12:1 force ratio north of the capital (RUSI) could not overcome poor tactical competence, no fallback plan, and Ukrainian artillery; the force withdrew in early April. Kharkiv (September 2022) and Kherson (November 2022) showed it could be outmanoeuvred when pinned and its supply interdicted. Gains since 2023 have come at very high casualty cost per km, and RUSI judges Russian units lose coordination quickly in dynamic situations.
